summary.judgment: The lesson has one clear move, a strong novice-facing retrieval gate, correct deterministic computations, five distinct explanatory visuals, exactly six exercises with complete solutions, exactly one forward exercise/Ref, and an excellent join from windows into the next stochastic-spectra lesson. It is not ready because the zero-padding theorem overclaims from underspecified hypotheses and the spectral-resolution definition omits the required learner-generated boundary prompt; several callouts fail the deletion test; all five 456-645-word content sections lack level-three segmentation; and the shipped figure typography violates the preflight's 12 px mobile floor.

rubric_items.evidence: The exact declarative opening states both capabilities and limits: ‘A sampled main lobe can locate one isolated tone between bins, but denser FFT samples do not add observation time or separate unresolved components.’
The first new formal identity follows a concrete fs=1024, N=64, q=10.31 Hann-windowed tone and the L=64 versus L=1024 comparison; the formula names what the record already demonstrated.

Every section serves the one decision boundary: unchanged-DTFT sampling, isolated-peak fitting, window-dependent fit error, phase-induced false peaks, then localization-versus-resolution action. No PSD/Welch, FFT-factorization, or window-metric detour appears.

At 4,349 words, the chapter includes an exact sampling identity, a worked frequency/amplitude estimate, estimator rejection boundaries, a deterministic error study, a two-tone phase counterexample, five visuals, and six fully solved exercises. It is textbook-substantial at this level.

The theorem says fixed products x[n]w[n] imply unchanged ‘record duration’ and the ‘window transform's main-lobe width in hertz,’ but it does not hypothesize fixed fs or fixed w, and its proof silently substitutes zeros/main-lobe width of X_w for those of the window transform. The exact DFT=DTFT-sample identity is proved, but the consequences do not follow from the stated hypotheses for arbitrary fixed windowed data. The spectral-resolution definition supplies canonical, different, degenerate, and near-miss cases but no learner-generated example/non-example prompt required by the math overlay.
rubric_items.action: State fixed N, fs>0, acquired x[n], and fixed window w[n]; keep the theorem conclusion to the exact sample identity, then give duration and W-main-lobe invariance as a scoped corollary. Add the missing learner-generated resolution/non-resolution prompt.
